newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kohler sees earnings up in tough market.
newsitem.headline: Kohler sees earnings up in tough market.

text.p: South African packaging firm Kohler Ltd said on Tuesday that it would continue to see improved earnings despite weak consumer demand and tough competition.

"Despite these difficulties, management is intensifying its efforts to improve efficiencies, contain cost increases and meet customer requirements and as a result anticipate that earnings will continue to improve," said Kohler chief executive Richard Bruyns.
Earlier the firm posted a first half earnings per share of 24.8 cents, up from 22.1 cents last time.
Total group earnings rose to 73.4 million rand compared to 64.1 million previously, while turnover was up to 1,231.9 million rand from 1,174.5 million.
Bruyns said demand for packaging products had been weak in the six month period to end February, but that a strong turnaround at its Kimberly-Clark consumer business had boosted results.
"Notwithstanding the slower consumer market, volume growth was good and Kimberly-Clark retained its dominant market shares in personal products," Bruyns said.
Consumer turnover rose to 259.8 million rand from 244.5 million rand while earnings there jumped to 16.2 million rand from 4.9 million rand.
However, packaging is still the dominant force in the group, contributing some 78 percent of earnings and 79 percent of turnover.

The packaging industry saw heavy pricing pressures and slow growth in volumes. As a result turnover only edged up to 972.1 million rand from 930.0 million rand, while earnings dropped to 57.2 million rand from 59.2 million rand.
Bruyns said the firm had been especially hit by increased competition in the Western Cape corrugated market.
"In packaging the markets for our products remained weak in the period, confirming the downward trend experienced in the second half of last year," he said.
In plastics packaging the group's markets showed marginal growth.
A restructuring at the firm's loss-making metal can division has now largely been completed, Bruyns said. A new can line is now operating, but had a late commissioning amid initial problems.
"Determined efforts continue to be made to return this company to profitability," he said.
